title: Changing Shapes of Solids
keyIdea: You can change the shape of some solid objects by squashing, stretching, bending or twisting them. Each one is a push or a pull. The shape changes but the material stays the same: squashed clay is still clay, and there is the same amount of it. Materials do not all act the same way. Dough and foil stay in their new shape, a sponge and an elastic band spring back when you let go, a wooden block is too hard to squash with your hands, and a dry twig snaps if you bend it too far.

kid: Some solids can change shape. You can squash dough flat. You can stretch an elastic band. You can bend a pipe cleaner. You can twist a wet cloth.
Squash means push down. Stretch means pull the ends apart. Bend means make a curve or a corner. Twist means turn the two ends opposite ways.
When clay gets a new shape, it is still clay. It is still the same amount of clay. It is just spread out in a new way.
Some things go back when you let go, like a sponge. Some stay in the new shape, like dough. A wooden block is too hard to squash. A dry twig snaps if you bend it a lot.
adult: This is a Year 2 science aim in England, in the unit called Uses of everyday materials. Children find out how the shapes of solid objects made from some materials can be changed by squashing, bending, twisting and stretching. It builds on Year 1 work on how materials feel. It leads on to pushes and pulls in Year 3.

Use the four words with care. Squashing pushes the ends together. Stretching pulls them apart. Bending makes a curve. Twisting turns the two ends in opposite ways. Then sort what you see. Some things change and stay changed, like dough, foil and a pipe cleaner. Some spring back when you let go, like a sponge, a band or a spring. A wooden block does not change with a child's push. A dry twig snaps.

Common mistakes to watch for. A child may think a flat or long lump has less clay because it looks thin. A child may think a new shape is a new material. Some call every change a squash. Some think any solid will bend if you try hard. Some mix up bending, which makes a curve, with twisting, which turns the ends.

In the lab your child drags to squash dough, stretch a band, bend a pipe cleaner and twist a cloth. They roll clay into new shapes on a scale that stays level. They guess, then test, a pipe cleaner, a dry twig, a wooden block and foil. They sort six things into goes back or stays changed, and name the action in jobs at home.

familyTip: Make a shape-changing tray: play dough, an elastic band, a sponge, a pipe cleaner, a sheet of foil and a lolly stick. Ask your child to squash, stretch, bend or twist each one, then let go. Which ones go back? Which one did not change at all?

visual.caption: Does it go back when you let go? Drag each thing, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: squash, stretch, bend and twist, weigh clay in new shapes, test which materials change or snap, and sort what springs back.

practice.prompt: You roll a ball of clay into a long snake. What is true?
choices: It is the same amount of clay
practice.hint: Did you add any clay or take any away? Or did you just change its shape?
practice.explain: Rolling only changes the shape. Nothing was added or taken away, so it is the same amount of clay.

practice.prompt: A ball of clay weighs the same as {n} cubes. You squash it flat. How many cubes does it weigh now?
practice.hint: Squashing changes the shape. Does it change how much clay there is?
practice.explain: It still weighs {n} cubes. The clay is spread out, but there is the same amount.

practice.prompt: You have {a} sponges and {b} lumps of dough. You squash them all, then let go. How many spring back?
practice.hint: Which one goes back when you let go: a sponge or dough?
practice.explain: Only the {a} sponges spring back. The {b} lumps of dough stay squashed.

practice.prompt: You hold both ends of a wet cloth and turn them opposite ways. What are you doing?
practice.hint: Turning the two ends opposite ways has its own word. It is how you wring out water.
practice.explain: Turning the ends opposite ways is twisting. Bending makes a curve, and stretching pulls the ends apart.

pool.prompt: Which one can you squash with your hands?
pool.hint: Which one feels soft when you press it?
pool.explain: Play dough is soft, so a push squashes it. Wood and metal spoons are too hard for your hands.

pool.prompt: You pull the ends of an elastic band apart. What are you doing?
pool.hint: Do the ends go further apart or closer together?
pool.explain: Pulling the ends apart is stretching. The band gets longer.

pool.prompt: You bend a dry twig a lot. What happens?
choices: It goes back like a band
pool.hint: A dry twig is stiff. What happens to stiff things when you bend them too far?
pool.explain: A dry twig is stiff and not bendy, so it snaps. A pipe cleaner bends and stays bent.

pool.prompt: Mia squashes a sponge and lets go. What happens?
pool.hint: Think of washing up. What does a sponge do after you squeeze it?
pool.explain: A sponge springs back to its shape when you stop squashing it.

pool.prompt: Sam makes his foil into a ball. Is it still foil?
choices: No, it is a new material
pool.hint: Did the stuff change, or only the shape?
pool.explain: Only the shape changed. Scrunched-up foil is still foil.

pool.prompt: There are {n} pipe cleaners. You bend each one into a hook. How many pipe cleaners are there now?
pool.hint: Bending changes the shape. Does it change how many there are?
pool.explain: There are still {n} pipe cleaners. Each one just has a new hook shape.

pool.prompt: You roll out pizza dough with a rolling pin. Which way are you changing it?
pool.hint: A rolling pin pushes down on the dough. Which word means push down?
pool.explain: The rolling pin pushes down, so you are squashing the dough flatter.

pool.prompt: Which one stays in its new shape after you let go?
pool.hint: Two of these spring back. Which one keeps its new shape?
pool.explain: A pipe cleaner has wire inside, so it stays bent. The band and the sponge go back.

pool.prompt: You test {s} sponges and {t} dry twigs by bending them. How many snap?
pool.hint: A sponge is soft and springy. A dry twig is stiff.
pool.explain: The {t} dry twigs snap. The {s} sponges bend and spring back.
